STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style tray with toast, a few cooked dark items, a piece of chocolate, and a mug of tea. It is photographed from a fairly high, near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The food sits on an oval paper plate about 20 cm across, so the area is about 314 cm². The sugar sachet is about 9 cm long, which fits this scale.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) two slices of toast, (b) about 3-4 small cooked dark mushrooms, (c) dark chocolate pieces. The tea in the mug and the sugar sachet are not counted.

STEP 4 - Area: Toast about 40% (126 cm²), mushrooms about 8% (25 cm²), chocolate about 6% (19 cm²). Total is about 54% of the plate, which is plausible for this sparse plating.

STEP 5 - Volume: Toast 126 cm² x 1.0 cm ≈ 126 ml. Mushrooms 25 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 38 ml. Chocolate 19 cm² x 0.8 cm ≈ 15 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Toast is set by slice weight (two slices ≈ 60 g), since bread bulk density gives a similar figure. Mushrooms 38 ml x 0.6 ≈ 23 g. Chocolate 15 ml x 0.9 ≈ 14 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Toast 60 g x 250 kcal/100 g = 150 kcal. Mushrooms 23 g x 30 kcal/100 g ≈ 7 kcal. Chocolate 14 g x 530 kcal/100 g ≈ 74 kcal. Total ≈ 97 g, ≈ 231 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 100 g of toast, mushrooms and chocolate is plausible for a light breakfast tray. Tea and sugar are excluded, so the total is slightly low if those are counted.
